summary: This is a sound, low-risk, single-kernel change whose act_and_mul row (14.2/14.7/52.9/52.2 us in fb1e52d2119d4175) can be read directly from the profile. The weakest link is its central premise, which is contradicted by master's own code: -1 routes ARE bucketed into sorted_ids[:n_padded] (in blocks whose block_experts entry is -1), so the 'fallback' mask is the real path, and the mechanism is wider tiles plus sorted-order L2 locality, not skipping remote slots that SGLang's kernel already skips.
justification: Profile check: act_and_mul_kernel is 14.2 us (turn_1 sliding), 14.7 (turn_1 full), 52.9 (turn_4 sliding), 52.2 (turn_4 full), 1.0-1.5% of each shape. It scales ~3.7x for 4x the tokens, so the cost is per-row work and not launch overhead. The local-row floor (~T rows x 24.6 KB at 4.8 TB/s = ~3.9 / ~15.4 us) is computed correctly, so SGLang's kernel runs at ~1.3 TB/s and a 2-D-tiled Triton elementwise kernel reaching 2.5-3.5 TB/s is plausible on H200. cache1 was just written by Marlin w13 (~12 MB of local rows at turn_1), so part of the read may come from L2, which makes ~5-6 us reachable. Expected directions match TASK.md: turn_1/turn_4 faster by ~0.7-0.8% of shape time, first_turn flat (T=16384 > MARLIN_MAX_TOKENS goes to _experts_triton, untouched). The hypothesis says honestly that this is inside the +-1.5% headline CI and must be judged on the kernel row. WEAKEST LINK: the claim that remote slots never appear in sorted_ids' valid range is contradicted by submission.py itself. _moe_nvfp4_gemm_kernel has an 'off_expert == -1' branch, and ZERO_NONLOCAL_W2's comment (line 181) says 'the m-blocks of non-local routes (expert -1)'. Marlin's is_ep path skips those blocks; it does not rely on them being absent. So the prepare() assert as written will fail and the local_ids-mask fallback is what gets built. Make that the primary design, not a fallback. Better still, exit early per row tile when block_experts[pos // block_size_m] == -1. In practice block_size_m is always 64 at every prefill T (the candidate loop never breaks before 64 for T >= 200: T*8/32/64 >= 0.78 at T=200, and it breaks at 64 or ends there). BLOCK_R=16 divides 64, so one block_experts load per program skips whole remote tiles without a per-row gather of local_ids. The consequence for the mechanism: SGLang's act_and_mul (expert_ids=local_ids, expert_step=1) already skips -1 rows, so 'it launches over all T*8 slots' is not what separates the two kernels. The new grid also covers ~T*8 + padding positions, most of them remote. The gain has to come from tile shape and occupancy (16 rows x 512 cols per CTA instead of SGLang's one row per block) and from sorted (expert-major) order matching Marlin's write order for L2 hits. Both are plausible but unmeasured, so the ~5-6 us target may come in nearer 8-10 us. Minor points: 'compile for both Marlin block sizes the turn shapes use' is a single size (64); a bit-for-bit check against CUDA expf-based silu may differ by 1 bf16 ulp under Triton's exp/sigmoid lowering, so allow <= 1 ulp (or compute exactly 1/(1+exp(-x)) in fp32 the way SGLang does) rather than hard-failing prepare().
confounders: experts-hybrid-marlin-turn-triton-first-turn: this sets the T<=4096 gate that makes _experts_marlin the only path the change touches. The change is confined to that branch, so the gate scopes the result rather than confounding it. With the gate reverted (all-Triton), the change would not run at the turn shapes at all.
experts-triton-w4a16-first-turn-blockt256 / swapab stages: _experts_triton (T>4096) keeps SGLang's silu_and_mul byte-identical, so the first_turn shapes are an in-run null control. No interaction.

sglang-pipeline-parity (routing remap to local_ids with -1): this defines the -1 contract the new kernel depends on. It does not confound the timing, but it is why the remote-slot handling must be a mask or block-level -1 exit and not an assumption.
interference: No companion is warranted. The result can be read directly: the act_and_mul_kernel row disappears and _silu_mul_sorted_kernel replaces it in the same profile, at the same shapes, against the same Marlin producer and consumer. The first_turn shapes are an untouched in-run control for drift. A gain or loss on the kernel row is attributable without an A/B. The headline can't show it at all (~0.7% vs +-1.5% CI), and no companion would change that. One caveat for whoever dispatches: prefill checks are spent and this would go out as a scored submit whose headline cannot move outside noise. Its value is the per-kernel row and a stackable turn-shape piece, so consider batching it with another turn-shape change, or running it as a check after the reset.
rules_flags: None blocking. Static grid from sorted_ids.shape[0], n_padded read on device with early exit: no host sync, graph-safe. bf16 in/out with fp32 math matches SGLang's activation precision. Nothing is cached from data.

Correctness (not a rules issue, but it would fail the run): implement remote-slot exclusion (block_experts == -1 tile exit and/or local_ids[s] >= 0 mask) unconditionally. The prepare() assert that -1 slots are absent from sorted_ids[:n_padded] will fail against master's own -1-block contract, and failing prepare costs the run.
open_questions: Does SGLang's moe_align_block_size with N_EXPERTS=256 and -1 ids place the -1 routes in contiguous trailing blocks (so a tile-level exit removes them almost for free), or scatter them? This decides whether the walk costs ~T*8 positions or ~T.
How much of cache1's local rows is still L2-resident after Marlin w13 at turn_4 (~49 MB of local rows, about L2 size)? This sets whether turn_4 can reach ~20 us or stays nearer 30 us.
Is the prepare() reference check bit-exact achievable given CUDA expf vs Triton exp lowering, or should it accept 1 bf16 ulp?
